---
title: "Error budgets under estimated pairwise probabilities"
subtitle: "4.14 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 15"
description: "Inner and outer feasible families under bounds on Monte Carlo coefficient error."
---

A report can satisfy an error budget on estimated pairwise probabilities and violate it under the stipulated exact
law. The budget concerns the expected wrong share among stated pairs. Given a proposed uniform bound on probability
error, tighter and looser estimated thresholds define inner and outer feasible families. The display checks the
coefficient bound and the resulting inclusions separately, alongside an advisory numerical tolerance. A fixed-size
independent-draw illustration distinguishes a probabilistic numerical error guarantee from the deterministic
membership calculations. Neither calculation establishes calibration of the supplied posterior model.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Estimated pass.** For A above B, the estimated wrong share is .200 and the exact supplied-law share is .300.
  The budget is .25. Its estimated row passes while its exact row fails; the inner threshold .15 and outer
  threshold .35 remain separate on the number line.
- **Negative inner.** The signed inner threshold is −.05, even though the estimated wrong share is 0. Replacing
  this threshold with zero would wrongly admit A above B. The all-withheld report still passes the count-form
  tests, with no defined wrong share.
- **Exactly two.** Requiring two grades removes all-withheld. The inner family has 0 reports; the exact family
  also happens to be empty here. Their separate counters matter: an empty inner family alone would not establish
  exact infeasibility.
- **Radius too small.** The proposed radius is reduced to .05 with the exact law unchanged.
  The coefficient checks read “no,” and an inner member fails the exact budget. The app displays the actual
  inclusion counterexample rather than assuming the bracket.
- **Raw comparisons.** With advisory tolerance removed, its coefficient check reads “no.” At the default radius,
  the tiny raw excess explains why the strict check fails while the tolerant comparison passes. The actual
  inclusions are separate tests, not consequences of accepting a soft tolerance.
- **Fixed-S IID.** The separate illustration uses 1,000 whole-state draws from the six-site independent normal
  law, reusing the Monte Carlo producer and bound. Score B has error weight 0 but remains protected by its .03
  budget. Requiring exactly two grades gives an empty inner family while the exact family remains nonempty.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
“Exact” means the stipulated supplied law. The main two-unit example declares coefficients deterministically and
makes no sampling-probability claim. In the IID illustration, the fixed-size simultaneous coefficient event has
probability at least one minus α across repeated numerical samples from the same law. This concerns numerical
approximation, not model calibration or a posterior probability of compliance. Signed thresholds are never clipped.
:::
